The test image shows a field of soybean plants with prominent yellow/golden mottling on leaves, especially in the upper canopy. No discrete lesions or fungal growth visible — pattern looks like mosaic/mottling. This is a leaf-level issue.

Top candidates from leaf classes: Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus (yellow mottling upper canopy), Downy_mildew, Sudden_death_syndrome.

Let me view reference images one at a time, starting with Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus.
This matches somewhat — light green/yellow mottling with some leaf distortion. Now check Downy_mildew.
Downy mildew shows small discrete yellowish spots, not the broad mottling seen in the test image. Let me check Sudden_death_syndrome.
SDS shows brown interveinal necrosis with visible dead tissue — not matching the test image. Let me check Soybean_Vein_necrosis_virus.
Vein necrosis shows discrete yellow-brown spots along veins — not matching the broad mottling. Let me check the second Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus reference.
Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus shows white/pale mottling. The test image has more golden-yellow tone. Let me check Brown_Stem_Rot leaf and Cercospora to cover other candidates.
I've viewed 7 reference images so far (need exactly 8). Let me check Soybean_Cyst_Nematode since it also causes yellowing.

The Soybean_Cyst_Nematode reference is nearly identical to the test image — same field-wide view with golden-yellow upper canopy leaves mixed with green. This is a strong match.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: field-wide view, upper canopy leaves with prominent golden-yellow coloring, no discrete spots/lesions/fungal growth
- SCN reference (Soybean_Dise_19): essentially the same pattern — golden-yellow leaves scattered throughout the upper canopy across the whole field
- Bean_Pod_Mottle_virus: showed more white/silvery mottling, not the golden-yellow tone
- Downy_mildew, SDS, Vein_necrosis, Brown_Stem_Rot, Cercospora: all eliminated by reference images showing very different symptom patterns
- SCN KB description confirms: "yellowing of leaves, stunting of plants, commonly appearing in circular or lens-shaped patterns in the field"
